Independent fresh pass · September 30, 2026

Vandalizer 5.0
UI, UX & usefulness for an RA

The core document workflow is useful and increasingly coherent. The broader app is not yet a consistent 8/10 experience: keyboard access, mobile supporting pages and discoverability need another focused pass.

7.3/10Visual UI
6.7/10User experience
7.5/10RA task fit

Unweighted average of 23 assessed RA-facing areas. Two supporting-role overviews are graded separately and excluded from that average. This is not an all-surfaces 8/10 sign-off.

PrioritiesScorecardSurface critiquesScreenshotsMethod & limits

What to preserve

The document → Library → run → retry → return journey passed at 1440, 1024, 768, 390 and 320px. The source document stayed in scope. Keep this split-pane model while improving labels and controls.

Prioritized findings

Three P1 groups deserve attention before another decorative polish pass. P2 items improve comprehension and everyday work; P3 improves consistency.

P1 · RA-01Confirmed

Workflow and activity navigation are not fully keyboard-operable

Workflow StepCard and ActivityRail rows are clickable divs without role, tabIndex or keyboard activation. DOM inspection of the workflow step confirmed tabIndex -1; pointer activation opened it.

RA impact: Keyboard users cannot reliably reach the same editing and resume actions as pointer users.

Change: Use a named keyboard-operable primary action for each row/card; preserve independent move and delete buttons.

Acceptance: Tab to a step and an activity item; Enter/Space opens the intended item; focus returns predictably after closing.

P1 · RA-02Confirmed

Team Admin and examiner layouts fail on narrow screens

At a 390px viewport the scrollable PageLayout container measured 878px wide in content. The fixed 220px sidebar leaves the KPI grid clipped. The examiner Shared items page uses the same fixed-width sidebar pattern; at 390px its explanation becomes a column of short word fragments and its search control is clipped.

RA impact: A team owner cannot read the overview in the initial phone viewport. A document-level overflow check missed this nested overflow.

Change: Collapse the sidebar at narrow widths and stack the KPI/chart grids; measure nested scroll containers in QA.

Acceptance: At 390px and 320px all primary labels, values and export controls are visible without horizontal page/container scrolling.

P1 · RA-03Confirmed

Accessibility coverage stops short of the surrounding app

Axe found an unnamed Reviews status select, an unnamed artifact-edit textarea and an unnamed Support close button. Docs mobile also has an unnamed button. Contrast failures appear in Reviews, Teams, Docs, Certification, Tuning, Admin and empty tool histories.

RA impact: Critical RA handoff and help actions are less accessible than the main workspace.

Change: Add associated labels and control names, repair contrast, and add these routes and editing states to the regular accessibility checks.

Acceptance: Named controls appear in accessibility snapshots; each listed state passes the relevant axe checks and a manual keyboard pass.

P2 · RA-04Confirmed

Failed activity emphasizes deletion over recovery

In the expanded activity capture, the failed workflow displays a yellow title row and a trailing delete control; the status icon shares the trailing area and is not clearly visible. Failure detail is carried in hover text.

RA impact: An RA scanning recent work can miss that something needs attention.

Change: Show a persistent Failed label and concise reason/recovery action; keep deletion in a separate location.

Acceptance: A failed run is recognizable without hover, color recognition or opening the item, on desktop and touch screens.

activity-populated

frontend/src/components/workspace/ActivityRail.tsx:349
P2 · RA-05Confirmed

The default workflow pane hides useful section labels

At the ordinary desktop split width, Design, Input, Validate, Advanced and History become five icons. The compact threshold is 520px. Left navigation also uses icons with hover titles rather than visible labels.

RA impact: The RA must learn two icon systems before discovering input setup and past results.

Change: Retain readable tab text through wrapping or compact labels and offer labeled navigation expansion. Keep the current document/tool split.

Acceptance: A first-time user can locate Input, History, Files and Knowledge without hovering or memorizing symbols; document context remains open.

P2 · RA-06Design critique

Projects do not immediately show the work to resume

Opening the sample project shows project-scoped chat. Files, members, status and pinned tools are primarily exposed through Manage project.

RA impact: A project feels more like a chat scope than a place to check progress and continue a submission.

Change: Expose a compact project overview or pinned-work summary inside the existing workspace; keep chat and tools available beside sources.

Acceptance: The user can identify project contents, current state and a next action without opening a settings-like dialog.

frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:998
P2 · RA-07Design critique

Automation header layout spends space on controls before the title

“Review incoming proposals” wraps into three lines beside Run now, Enabled, Private, delete and close in the desktop editor.

RA impact: The primary identity of the open automation becomes harder to scan than its action controls.

Change: Give the title its own flexible row and group actions beneath it when the pane narrows.

Acceptance: Ordinary three-to-six-word titles stay readable at the default split and laptop widths without hiding actions.

automation-detail

frontend/src/components/workspace/AutomationEditorPanel.tsx
P2 · RA-08Design critique

Help starts with deployment, not RA work

The Docs Getting Started screen shows repository cloning, Docker and server commands. The workspace task guidance uses knowledge-base and workflow concepts earlier than some newcomers will understand.

RA impact: An RA seeking help with a proposal may conclude the product expects developer knowledge.

Change: Add a direct RA quickstart: upload a proposal, identify requirements, verify a source, save or share the result. Retain deployment docs in their existing topic.

Acceptance: An RA reaches a relevant worked example from help without passing through installation instructions.

docs-top · chat-onboarding

frontend/src/pages/Docs.tsx:46frontend/src/pages/Docs.tsx:92
P2 · RA-09Design critique / data-dependent scenario

Validation and catalog setup still demand expert interpretation

Validation combines question authoring, quality checks, retrieval improvement and tuning controls. In the catalog missing-metadata fixture, input and expected output remain unspecified even while a quality score is visible.

RA impact: Users can understand a score without understanding whether the tool fits their actual task.

Change: Lead with a representative task and example deliverable; summarize what the test established and what needs review. Require or strongly prompt input/output examples for shared tools.

Acceptance: A colleague can choose a tool and explain its input, output and test scope before running it.

knowledge-validation · catalog-detail

P3 · RA-10Design critique

Visual language varies between tools and supporting pages

The purple/checkerboard workflow canvas, blue support widget, yellow workspace and dark Docs site have different visual emphasis and control treatments.

RA impact: Cross-surface transitions feel less cohesive, even when the functions work.

Change: Align typography, action hierarchy, spacing and state treatments; retain distinctive diagrams only where they explain behavior.

Acceptance: The same class of action and status is recognizable across workspace, Reviews, Support and learning.

workflow-step · support-form · docs-top

Critique by surface

Workspace navigation

UI 7.5 · UX 6.5 · RA usefulness 7.5

Works: The document and tool panes work together; the redundant split icon is gone.

Critique: Left navigation still requires recognition of five icons. Workflow section labels disappear at the default split width. Add persistent or expandable labels without changing the pane model.

files · file-library-tool-1440

Public entry and sign-in

UI 8.0 · UX 7.5 · RA usefulness 7.0

Works: The landing page has a strong hierarchy and a clear sign-in path.

Critique: The first screen sells platform breadth rather than a concrete RA outcome. “Verified workflows” also differs from the in-app “shared” and “checked” language. Authentication submission was not exercised.

landing · sign-in

First-session guidance

UI 8.0 · UX 7.5 · RA usefulness 7.5

Works: Upload, chat, a sample demo and a tour provide several ways to start.

Critique: The page still asks the newcomer to choose a knowledge base or build a workflow. Lead with one short proposal-review example and let tool concepts follow the task.

chat-onboarding

Chat and document/KB scope

UI 8.0 · UX 8.0 · RA usefulness 8.0

Works: Attached scope and source-health warnings are visible. Upload scope is preserved in the outgoing request. Citations and export are available.

Critique: A source link is useful, but this short synthetic answer does not establish claim-level grounding on real sponsor documents. Keep evidence inspection close to each important answer.

chat-kb-answer · chat-file-attached

Agent approvals and recovery

UI 8.0 · UX 7.5 · RA usefulness 8.0

Works: The approval names the action, previews the change and offers an explicit cancellation. Completion offers an Open workflow action.

Critique: Old approval messages remain in the transcript after the result. Clearer historical status and a compact final result would reduce the amount an RA must reread. No real tool execution was tested.

chat-agent-confirmation · chat-agent-complete

Files and document-to-tool work

UI 8.0 · UX 8.0 · RA usefulness 8.5

Works: Opening a file, finding a Library workflow, retrying a failed run and returning to the document passed at five widths. The selected document UUID survived both run attempts.

Critique: File rows mainly communicate title and date. A richer document fixture is needed to judge scanned-PDF reading, tables and long-document navigation. Preserve the working split-pane interaction.

file-library-tool-1440 · file-library-run-complete-1440

Projects and collaboration

UI 7.5 · UX 6.5 · RA usefulness 7.5

Works: Project scope is prominent; Manage project exposes files, lifecycle state, pinned tools and members.

Critique: Opening a project lands on chat. Its contents and collaboration controls require a separate Manage action. A small persistent project overview could make this a better place to resume work without replacing the current panes.

project-detail · project-manage

Library organization

UI 7.5 · UX 7.0 · RA usefulness 8.0

Works: Mine, Team and Explore distinguish ownership and reuse. Search, type filters, saved views and folders support repeated work.

Critique: The user must distinguish workflows, extractions, prompts and formatters before deciding what to use. Add task-oriented entry points alongside the existing organization.

library · library-mobile

Explore and shared tool detail

UI 8.0 · UX 7.0 · RA usefulness 7.5

Works: The detail panel exposes sample size, date, recorded quality and limits on what the score establishes.

Critique: The fixture with missing input/output descriptions is honest but leaves the RA unable to judge fit without opening the tool. Make an example input and expected deliverable part of publishing guidance. This is a missing-metadata scenario, not a finding about the live catalog.

catalog-detail

Workflow design, input and output

UI 7.0 · UX 5.5 · RA usefulness 8.0

Works: The workflow stays beside its document, shows input scope and exposes an output with Download and Save to folder.

Critique: Step cards are pointer-only controls; the main editor tabs become icons at the ordinary split width. Nested step/task editing adds substantial conceptual load. Fix keyboard access first, then improve labels and starter-task guidance.

file-library-tool-1440 · workflow-step

Extraction design, results and evidence

UI 7.5 · UX 7.0 · RA usefulness 8.5

Works: A field result links to its source and keeps the document beside the extraction. Export is visible when results exist.

Critique: A single-field example is clear; bulk multi-document comparison and export fidelity still need real-data testing. Result inspection also copies the value, coupling two actions that users may not expect.

extraction-result · extraction-source

Automations: list, setup and history

UI 7.5 · UX 7.5 · RA usefulness 8.5

Works: Trigger, input, action and output summaries make each automation understandable. The wizard supports saving disabled. Recorded output is available in history.

Critique: The editor title wraps to three lines while controls compete for the same row. Keep title and action groups on separate responsive rows. The list should remain the clear monitoring surface.

automation-detail · wizard-5-activation · automation-output

Knowledge bases and source health

UI 8.0 · UX 7.5 · RA usefulness 8.5

Works: Partial readiness, failed sources and the distinction between availability and validation are explicit. Chat and source management are close together.

Critique: Source cards can become tall and repetitive. With a large policy collection, compact health summaries and a clear “needs attention” view would matter more than another badge. Large-collection behavior was not measured in this pass.

knowledge-detail · knowledge-mobile

Validation and quality improvement

UI 7.0 · UX 6.5 · RA usefulness 7.5

Works: Test questions, expected answers, baseline comparisons and history provide a useful basis for evaluating reusable work.

Critique: Validation has several layers of tabs and substantial explanatory copy. “Improve retrieval,” model/grader choices and tuning budgets remain expert concepts. Make the default path a small representative test with an actionable summary; keep detailed controls available. Scores in this review are synthetic.

Activity and resuming work

UI 7.0 · UX 5.5 · RA usefulness 7.0

Works: Recent work is accessible without leaving the workspace and links back to the corresponding tool.

Critique: The failed-run row makes deletion more visually prominent than failure status. Activity rows also use pointer-only divs. Add keyboard-operable row actions and persistent status text, with deletion separated from status.

Human review queue and decision

UI 7.0 · UX 6.0 · RA usefulness 8.5

Critique: The status filter lacks an accessible name; the artifact-edit textarea is unnamed. Active-tab and action contrast also fail automated checks. This high-value RA surface needs the same care as the workspace. Decision submission was not exercised.

Account and team management

UI 7.5 · UX 7.0 · RA usefulness 7.5

Works: Profile, memory explanation, email preferences, member roles and invitation controls are understandable.

Critique: A global Member role and team Owner role appear on different pages without much distinction. Team management has a long sequence of equally styled cards; separate routine collaboration from ownership and deletion controls more clearly.

account · teams

Credentials and integrations

UI 7.0 · UX 6.0 · RA usefulness 5.5

Works: The form has labeled fields, disabled incomplete actions and a clear description of secret handling.

Critique: API Node IDs, static headers and OAuth client credentials are integration-specialist concepts. The generic account-menu placement makes this appear equally relevant to ordinary RAs. Keep it available with clearer purpose and audience framing. No secrets were entered or tested.

credentials-form

Support panel

UI 7.0 · UX 6.5 · RA usefulness 7.0

Works: The workspace remains visible while the user describes a problem. Subject, priority and description are straightforward.

Critique: The close button is unnamed. The blue floating panel introduces a different visual treatment, and category/priority selection adds work before the user describes the issue. No ticket was sent.

support-form

Certification and learning

UI 7.0 · UX 6.5 · RA usefulness 7.0

Works: A dockable course lets users learn beside their work. Duration and progress are explicit.

Critique: XP, tiers, locked modules and several docking icons dominate the course overview. The 3.5-hour curriculum should complement a short task-based first success. Only the overview and first lesson were inspected; course completion was not tested.

Docs and self-service help

UI 6.5 · UX 5.5 · RA usefulness 5.5

Works: Documentation is extensive and includes distinct topics and audience presentation links.

Critique: Getting Started immediately presents git clone, Docker, backend and frontend commands. That is a poor default help path for an RA already using the app. The dark site also has multiple contrast and mobile control issues. Add a visible RA quickstart with task walkthroughs.

Recommended next pass

  1. Fix P1 keyboard, mobile-layout and named-control failures before spending another pass on decoration.
  2. Keep the passing file → Library → run → recover → return journey intact at 1440, 1024, 768, 390 and 320px.
  3. Then improve labels, project resumption, failure visibility and RA help. Re-review affected states rather than rebuilding a giant screenshot matrix.
  4. Validate usefulness with real RAs on five tasks: identify a proposal deadline, compare a budget requirement, verify an extracted value, run a reusable checklist, and hand the result to a colleague. Record unaided completion, time, errors, evidence verification and whether the handoff is usable.

Method, coverage and limits

Production frontend served locally; Playwright Chromium with synthetic API fixtures. Fresh heuristic review, screenshots, DOM/keyboard semantics inspection and axe scans. No live model or backend execution.

UI: Hierarchy, readability, spacing, visual consistency and responsive layout.

UX: Discoverability, keyboard access, scope retention, recovery and completion paths.

RA: Observable fit for research-administration tasks, evidence inspection, reuse and handoff. Not measured AI accuracy or demonstrated time savings.

SCALE: 9 exceptional; 8 strong with small friction; 7 useful with noticeable friction; 6 substantial learning or accessibility cost; 5 a serious limitation on the tested surface. Half-point grades are reviewer judgments, not precision measurements.

140 captures were recorded, including corrected attempts and repeated states; 129 non-blocked unique capture IDs remain in the evidence index. Automated checks found no violations in the 55-state core suite or the 30-state file-to-Library suite. Broader captures found issues documented above. No uncaught page errors were recorded. Zero axe violations does not establish full accessibility; manual inspection found pointer-only controls.

  • Every major RA-facing area was sampled, including account/team, support, reviews, learning and the Team Admin overview. Examiner and support-staff overviews were sampled separately. This is not an exhaustive audit of every configuration/admin tab.
  • No live authentication submission, model quality, permissions enforcement, delivery/email, real collaborator handoff, long/scanned PDF behavior, extraction export fidelity or production latency was validated.
  • Returning-user fixture has sparse activity and a small catalog. Empty-state and short-result quality cannot establish dense production usability.
  • Initial missing fixtures, wrong test selectors, expected role denial on /support and the first inconsistent extraction-source fixture were harness limitations, excluded from product findings. Corrected captures are used where available.
  • The previous split-icon removal is included in this build. No application code was changed for this assessment. No GitHub issues were reopened or created.
